info.title: Transcode
info.description: Transcode is the video and podcast conversion side of Navigatorr: workers (machines that encode), durable actions (one file, a batch of files, podcast ad cleaning), encoding recipes, candidates and promotion backups. The API reads what exists and what is happening, and writes: starting, cancelling, resuming and retrying actions, recording decisions, changing a batch goal, pausing and draining workers, changing worker slots, saving, deleting and rolling back recipes, cleaning, restoring and discarding backups, classifying and reviewing podcasts, revoking ad references and closing review-queue entries. A write calls the same function as the MCP tool or maintenance route of the same name and keeps every safeguard of it: expected revisions, digests and versions, confirm flags, dry-runs and idempotency keys are passed through, never bypassed (a request that omits one is refused with 400 or 409 exactly as the tool would, or answers the read-only preview). Start with GET /transcode/v1/workers to see the machines, GET /transcode/v1/actions?status=running to see what is encoding, and GET /transcode/v1/actions/{id} for one conversion. Paths use {id} for an action, batch or review-queue id, {name} for a worker or recipe. Lists are offset-based: send offset and limit, follow next_offset until has_more is false (/history is the exception: the audit log has no offset, it answers count and records). Write bodies are JSON (Content-Type: application/json, at most 1 MiB, unknown fields rejected). Errors are JSON {error, code, hint}; the hint names the endpoint to use instead. Authentication: X-Api-Key (or Authorization: Bearer) with the transcode API key, which needs nothing else for a write; a signed-in web console session may write only with the console's own write checks (header X-Navigatorr-Request: 1 and a same-site Origin). This document is public.

get.summary: List the workers with their health
get.description: Every transcode worker (a machine that encodes) as a row, plus a summary at the top. Call this first to see which workers exist, whether each is reachable and ready, why it is not (message, admission_note, scheduler_health), whether it is paused (pause) and which builds hold it. The observation field is the shared worker reachability, readiness and scheduler-sweep evidence (what the worker_health tool returned). Reads stored state and a cached probe; it never starts or restarts work. Read-only.
